key_insight: The paper shows that physics-informed neural operator training becomes practical and accurate when the residual loss is preconditioned to remove the severe mesh-dependent ill-conditioning caused by differential operators.
engineering_relevance: This enables label-free operator learning directly from governing equations, reducing offline data generation cost while preserving accuracy for PDE surrogates in scientific computing workflows.
method: Replace the standard physics-informed residual with a preconditioned residual loss.
Use geometric or algebraic multigrid to realize the preconditioner for linear and nonlinear PDEs.
Apply the approach across structured and unstructured meshes, with no added inference cost.
evidence_signal: On Poisson, Allen-Cahn, and stationary Stokes problems, the method matches supervised training and is reported to be 4–25× more accurate than prior physics-informed operator learning methods.
watch_item: The multigrid-based preconditioning must be implemented carefully for each discretization and PDE type, especially for saddle-point systems and refined meshes.
